clue.text: Force with long limbs?

definitions.meaning: a military force, a body of soldiers
a jokey adjective formed like 'leggy', describing someone well endowed with arms

explanation.definitionFit: A land fighting force is the commonest sense; the second is a playful coinage for having prominent upper limbs.

clue.text: Change row, about to exit

indicators.note: to exit means to leave, so the letter for about drops out of the quarrel word

parts.note: a row (rhyming with cow) is a noisy quarrel or altercation
C stands for circa, Latin for about, used before dates

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a change to a row of seats, or to an argument, before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: making a modification to something is effecting a change in it.

clue.text: Lizard's egg eaten by African

indicators.note: eaten by puts the egg word inside the African word, as if swallowed

parts.note: a Moor is a North African of Berber or Arab descent
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: A lizard's egg is devoured by someone in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the monitor is a large tropical lizard, such as the Komodo dragon.

clue.text: Coarse fabrics wrapping playwright's ivory carvings

indicators.note: wrapping says the fabric word goes round the playwright's name

parts.note: scrim is a coarse open-weave fabric used for curtains and theatre gauzes
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A playwright's ivory carvings are packed in rough cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrimshaw is carved or engraved work on ivory or whalebone, made by sailors.

clue.text: Saucer cat licked for seafood

indicators.note: licked in the sense of beaten or knocked about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A cat cleans a saucer that held fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'licked' looks like the cat finishing its saucer, but it signals that SAUCER CAT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Crustaceans such as crabs and lobsters are eaten as shellfish, a loose but fair stand-in for seafood.

clue.text: According to the book, twins' dad regularly tips balance

definitions.text: According to the book, twins' dad

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Rules say a parent of twins tends to tip the balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the book' is the Bible: in Genesis, the twins Jacob and Esau were sons of Isaac and Rebekah.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical knowledge: Genesis names the patriarch as father of the twins Esau and Jacob.

clue.text: With intentional public leaks, organise press release about Manx cat?

parts.note: to stage an event is to organise it

indicators.note: release suggests the letters are let loose and freed into a new arrangement
a Manx cat has no tail, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

explanation.surface: A publicist arranges a press release about a tailless cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' means tailless (Manx cats have none), docking WHIP to WHI; mixed with PRESS that gives WHISPERS. 'about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical term: an actor's aside meant to be heard by the audience is designed to leak openly.

clue.text: Forgetful inebriated man is shown up in the city

indicators.note: an inebriated man is reeling, so his letters stagger into another order
in places the turned word within the city abbreviation

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the word is written upwards, from the bottom

explanation.surface: A drunk is too forgetful to be seen in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inebriated' mixes MAN into AMN; 'shown up' turns IS to SI, which goes 'in' EC, the City of London's postcode, giving ESIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone suffering memory loss, as from drink, is forgetful.

clue.text: Biblical character's to mount horse

parts.note: to mount a jewel is to set it
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A Bible figure prepares to climb onto a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in Genesis the third son of Adam and Eve is a biblical character.

clue.text: Container with content of Famous Grouse, it may appear?

parts.note: a tin is a container

indicators.note: the content of a word is what lies inside its outer letters

explanation.surface: A tin holding a well-known Scotch whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: The Famous Grouse is a Scotch whisky, but here grouse is a game bird; the definition says the answer looks like one.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the South American tinamou is a ground bird that resembles a grouse or partridge.

clue.text: On paper, mum's almost unaffected by it whereas dad is

definitions.text: On paper, mum's almost unaffected by it whereas dad is

parts.words: On paper, mum's almost unaffected by it whereas dad is
parts.note: written backwards and mirrored, the letters m and u look nearly the same, while d turns into b

explanation.definitionFit: Script written right to left with letters reversed, as Leonardo did, alters some words visibly and others barely.

clue.text: Opposed to investment of profits in Laotian capital

indicators.note: investment in its old sense of clothing or enclosing, so the money unit surrounds the profits

parts.note: the at is a Laotian monetary unit, a hundredth of a kip
gains are profits

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to invest gains in Vientiane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laotian capital' reads as Vientiane but means money: the at is a coin of Laos.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being against a proposal is being opposed to it.

clue.text: We may get you back on the rails

definitions.text: We may get you back on the rails

parts.words: We may get you back on the rails
parts.note: on the rails suggests sorting out a wayward life, but it means by train: travel documents for the homeward leg

explanation.definitionFit: Railway tickets covering the outward and homeward journeys let a traveller come back by train.

clue.text: Walk around dull national landmark

indicators.note: around says the walking word goes round the word for dull

parts.note: to march is to walk in step
blear means dim or dull, as in bleary eyes

explanation.surface: A stroll around a tedious national monument.
explanation.walkthrough: MARBLE ARCH is a triumphal arch in London, near Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the white triumphal arch at Hyde Park's corner is a famous London landmark.

clue.text: Body's approximate temperature, taken earlier

indicators.note: taken earlier puts the temperature letter before the approximation

parts.note: or so means approximately, as in ten or so

explanation.surface: A patient's rough temperature was recorded beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the trunk of the human frame, without head or limbs, is the body.

clue.text: More than just a tea dance

definitions.text: More than just a tea dance

parts.words: More than just a tea dance
parts.note: cha is a word for tea, so more than one cha, three of them, makes the name of a Latin dance

explanation.definitionFit: A lively Latin American ballroom dance whose name repeats the slang word for tea three times.

clue.text: Rave about dummy hand that may not come into play?

definitions.text: that may not come into play?

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of the first word are shuffled

parts.note: in bridge the dummy's cards are laid out on the table, and the dummy is called the table

explanation.surface: Someone raves about the dummy's hand at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges RAVE to AVER; in bridge the dummy is laid face up and is called the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be prevented may never happen, never coming into play.

clue.text: Warped apart in a material sense

definitions.text: Warped apart in a material sense

parts.words: Warped apart in a material sense
parts.note: warp is the lengthwise thread in cloth, so a fabric whose threads are spaced apart is described

explanation.definitionFit: A loose textile with gaps between the threads, so its warp lies apart, is a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Flexible transaction set up on limited credit

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards

parts.note: a sale is a transaction

indicators.note: limited means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A deal arranged on restricted credit terms is flexible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns SALE into ELAS; 'limited' docks TICK to TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that stretches and gives, physically or in terms, is flexible.

clue.text: In evacuated suburb, leave without time to find explosive

indicators.note: In puts the departing word inside the emptied suburb
evacuated means emptied, leaving only the first and last letters
without says the time letter is dropped

parts.note: to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone flees an emptied suburb before an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' empties SUBURB to SB; 'without' takes T from QUIT, leaving QUI, which goes 'In' SB.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a squib is a small firework that hisses and bangs, an explosive.

clue.text: Public service shows lack of effectiveness: head sacked

indicators.note: head sacked removes the first letter, as a boss is fired

parts.note: futility is uselessness or lack of effect

explanation.surface: A public body proves useless, so its chief is fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a utility is a company supplying gas, water or electricity to the public.

clue.text: One getting into bed with haste, all excited?

definitions.text: One getting into bed with haste, all excited?

indicators.note: all excited says the letters are stirred up together

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone eager jumps into bed in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: someone hurrying into bed may be having an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an extramarital affair, the lover being someone tumbling into bed eagerly.

clue.text: Additional radiotherapy's incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete means the word loses letters at both ends, leaving an inner run

explanation.surface: A course of radiation treatment is unfinished, requiring more.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an additional item is a further or alternative one.

clue.text: South African spinner, short of length, misses wicket

indicators.note: misses means goes without, so the wicket letter goes too
short of means lacking, so the length letter goes

parts.note: in cricket a spinner is a slow bowler
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A South African spin bowler drops short and fails to take a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a ball pitched 'short of a length' bounces too early; here it removes L, and 'misses' removes W, from BOWLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Afrikaner of Dutch descent is a South African.

clue.text: Pound short, couldn't get full-flavoured bird

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the pound letter goes

parts.note: someone who lost could not get the prize
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pound
rich means full-flavoured, of food

explanation.surface: Lacking a pound, someone misses out on a tasty fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the large flightless African ostrich is a bird.

clue.text: With more to do, little time to climb in to tight clothing

indicators.note: to climb in says the time letter goes into the other word

parts.note: someone with more to do is busier
T is a little abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A busy person barely has time to squeeze into a figure-hugging garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bustier is a close-fitting strapless bodice, a piece of tight clothing.

clue.text: A hint of danger in a horticultural feature in. Hatton?

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'A hint of danger in a horticultural feature in. Hatton?': the stray full stop and 'A hint of danger' fit no parse of ROCK GARDEN; the clue looks garbled by OCR and the scan is blank.
annotationWithheld.clue: A hint of danger in a horticultural feature in. Hatton?

clue.text: Story girl's read out with tongue between teeth

indicators.text: read out with tongue between teeth
indicators.note: read out with tongue between teeth means said aloud with a lisp, turning s into th

parts.note: Miss is a title for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl reads a story aloud through clenched teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: A lisp turns the s sounds of MISS into th, giving the word for a legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a traditional tale or legend is a story.
